executiveSummary: The week's net movement was toward a genuinely two-track Gulf conflict rather than simple escalation: Iran extended its claim/attempt pattern to an unmanned US asset and third-country (Omani) waters while, for the first time since February, Iran and the six GCC states scheduled a direct ministerial dialogue (14 Sep, Salalah) reportedly floating a territorial-waters transit arrangement for Hormuz. That diplomatic opening arrived alongside, not instead of, hard confirmation that U.S. Gulf posture is durably degraded — Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao's on-record admission of Bahrain base damage, corroborated by open-source reporting putting rebuild costs near $400M with no return timeline. Independent AIS-based shipping trackers (Kpler, Lloyd's List) converged for the first time around a ~12-13 ships/day Hormuz baseline, narrowing but not resolving the gap with insurance-based 'effectively closed' readings. On the industrial side, the rare-earth chokepoint held at its already-escalated severity with no new PRC action, but three converging demand vectors (DPA-driven munitions ramp, the CVN-81 steam-catapult reversal, and now Iran's capture and expected reverse-engineering of a defective Anduril Dive-LD UUV) compounded its organizational significance. Cyber risk concentrated further on perimeter/identity infrastructure: the MikroTik 'MikroTrick' chain finally joined KEV (closing an 8-day gap) even as a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) Cisco Firewall Management Center bypass and a Citrix NetScaler flaw arrived under a hard 12 Sep federal patch deadline — six vendor families added to KEV in three weeks. CMMC's internal DoW CIO determination window (11-13 Sep) closed with no public output, converting a soft expectation into a confirmed information gap through the ~28 Sep public report. For an enterprise-tech/security leader, the week's throughline is that diplomatic openings and data-quality improvements are real but partial — the underlying assurance burden (patch now, maintain CMMC controls through the gap, revalidate Gulf contingency posture) has only grown.
whatChanged: Iran's claim/attempt pattern extended to an unmanned US asset (Saildrone-type UUV, 11 Sep) and to projectile strikes on two vessels off Oman (UKMTO), while the war's first GCC-Iran ministerial dialogue was scheduled for 14 Sep in Salalah, reportedly floating a territorial-waters Hormuz transit arrangement.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed on the record that Iranian strikes 'blew the hell out of' NSA Bahrain; open-source reporting (WSJ, via secondary coverage) documents command-headquarters and satellite-communications damage with a rebuild estimate near $400M and no return timeline.

Independent Hormuz-transit trackers (Kpler ~13/day 10-day avg; Lloyd's List Intelligence ~12/day) converged for the first time, narrowing but not resolving the gap with the war-risk-insurance-based 'effectively closed' reading and a lower single-day (7 transits) figure.

CMMC's internal DoW CIO Reform Task Force determination window (~11-13 Sep) closed with no public output identified, confirming a genuine two-plus-week information gap to the ~28 Sep public report; DFARS 7012/7021, SPRS, and annual affirmations remain fully binding throughout.

Cyber KEV cohort widened to six vendor families in three weeks: CISA formally listed the MikroTik 'MikroTrick' chain (CVE-2026-67277, CVE-2026-86060) on 10 Sep, while a CVSS-10.0 Cisco Firewall Management Center bypass (CVE-2026-20079) and Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490, CVSS 9.3) carry a 12 Sep federal patch deadline.

New thread opened: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy recovered a defective, 'dead in the water' Anduril Dive-LD UUV near Hormuz; CENTCOM/Anduril say no classified payload or sensitive data was aboard, but analysts expect an Iranian reverse-engineering effort against the hardware itself.

Army Secretary vacancy persisted 10 days without a formal nomination; the candidate field widened (Army Undersecretary Mike Obadal, Comptroller Marc Andersen, Rep. Brian Mast) alongside reported frontrunner Sean Parnell, whose confirmation prospects now carry a disclosed prior family-court finding.

Ukraine's 3-day capital-strike pause lapsed on schedule (8 Sep) with a mass Russian attack on Kyiv that NATO's Rutte called the highest civilian toll since May 2022; a separate, narrower 30-day energy-infrastructure strike-halt commitment (from the 7 Sep Trump-Putin call) remains neither confirmed nor violated, with Ukraine's deepest-yet drone strike (~3,000km) hitting a Russian gas complex and a Russian drone briefly entering Moldovan airspace.

trendsEmerging.soWhat: Vendors' 'no sensitive data' assurances need to separately address hardware-capture/reverse-engineering exposure, a distinct risk category from data loss.
